The '''2018–19 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 105th competitive season, 30th consecutive season in the top flight of English football, 27th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]], and 113th year in existence as a football club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history|website=chelseafc.com|date=1 July 2018}}</ref> The season covers the period from 1 July 2018 to 30 June 2019.

==Overview==
===August===
Chelsea began the league campaign under new manager Sarri with a "comfortable" 3–0 victory at Huddersfield Town,<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45067371 | title=Sarri's Chelsea too good for Huddersfield | work=BBC Sport }}</ref> with new midfielder Jorginho scoring a penalty on his debut, in between goals from N'Golo Kante and Pedro. This was followed by a home clash with Arsenal in the first home match of the season. After Pedro and Alvaro Morata quickly established a firm Chelsea advantage, Arsenal fought back to level before the break before Marcos Alonso won it late for the Blues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/38321|title = Chelsea v Arsenal, 2018/19 &#124; Premier League}}</ref>
Chelsea then made the long trip to Newcastle, and took the lead with fourteen minutes to play with an Eden Hazard penalty. With seven minutes to play, striker Joselu leveled it up, however Chelsea would have the last word, with a DeAndre Yedlin own goal with three minutes left seeing them edge it 2–1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/38334|title = Newcastle v Chelsea, 2018/19 |website=Premier League}}</ref>

===September===
Chelsea began September by earning their fourth successive league win, courtesy of a 2–0 triumph over Bournemouth after goals from  Pedro and Hazard late on.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/38341|title = Chelsea v AFC Bournemouth, 2018/19 &#124; Premier League}}</ref> This was followed by a clash with Cardiff City, but Chelsea were silenced after a surprise early goal from Sol Bamba; however two goals in six minutes from Hazard ensured Chelsea took a 2–1 lead, before he completed his hat-trick ten minutes from time. A Willian goal soon afterwards sealed a 4–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/38349|title = Chelsea v Cardiff, 2018/19 &#124; Premier League}}</ref>
This was followed by a trip to Greek outfit PAOK Salonika in the opening group stage contest of that season's UEFA Europa League, with Chelsea playing in the competition for the first time since winning it in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2010095--benfica-vs-chelsea/|title=Benfica-Chelsea &#124; UEFA Europa League 2012/13|website=[[UEFA]]|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> The Blues started off their campaign brightly, scoring after just seven minutes through Willian, but ultimately had to battle to a 1–0 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/paok-snika-vs-chelsea/report/401937|title=PAOK 0-1 Chelsea: Willian scores winner in Europa League clash|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> However, Chelsea dropped their first points of the campaign against a West Ham team that had been winless at home thus far that season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/west-ham-united-results/2018-19|title=West Ham United (Sky Sports)|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> drawing 0–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/west-ham-vs-chelsea/390816|title = West Ham 0-0 Chelsea: Maurizio Sarri's winning run ends at London Stadium}}</ref>
Chelsea followed the point at the London Stadium with a League Cup third-round success at Liverpool. After falling behind on 56 minutes through Daniel Sturridge, Chelsea struck back through Emerson and Hazard to claim a 2–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/liverpool-vs-chelsea/401814|title = Liverpool 1-2 Chelsea: Eden Hazard scores stunner in comeback}}</ref> They then faced a Reds side with a stronger team sheet at Stamford Bridge in the league, but were undone thanks to a late Sturridge stunner, and had to settle for a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-liverpool/390820|title = Chelsea 1-1 Liverpool: Daniel Sturridge scores superb equaliser|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> However, with Hazard having scored five league goals in the month, including the hat-trick against Cardiff, he was awarded with the Premier League Player of the Month for September 2018.<ref name="premierleague.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/stats/awards?se=210&aw=-1|title = Premier League Awards - Player, Manager & Goal of the Month|website=Premierleague.com}}</ref>

===October===
October began with a narrow win over Hungarians MOL Vidi in the Europa League, with Morata scoring the game's only goal with twenty minutes to play.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-vidi/report/401950|title=Chelsea 1-0 MOL Vidi: Alvaro Morata volley secures unconvincing win|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea then turned on the style in a 3–0 league win at Southampton, with Ross Barkley scoring his first of the season in between Hazard and Morata goals.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/soton-vs-chelsea/390834|title = Southampton 0-3 Chelsea: Ross Barkley finds form as Blues march on| newspaper=Sky Sports }}</ref> Next up, Jose Mourinho – who had won three Premier League titles with Chelsea – made his return to Stamford Bridge as manager of Manchester United,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/managers/2663/Jos%C3%A9-Mourinho/overview|title=José Mourinho Manager Profile, Record & Stats &#124; Premier League|website=Premierleague.com|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> who were eighth in the league and struggling.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=210&ha=-1|title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives|website=Premierleague.com|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea took a 1–0 lead into half-time after a looping header from Antonio Rudiger, but a quickfire double from Anthony Martial in the second half put United in front; however, a 96th-minute equalizer from Ross Barkley kept Chelsea's unbeaten season intact.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-man-utd/report/390840|title=Chelsea 2-2 Manchester United: Last-gasp Ross Barkley goal saves Chelsea|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>
Chelsea maintained their perfect Europa League record after a hat-trick for Ruben Loftus-Cheek helped them to a 3–1 win over Belarusian BATE Borisov,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-bate-borisov/401972|title = Chelsea 3-1 BATE Borisov: Ruben Loftus-Cheek hat-trick steers Blues to comfortable win}}</ref> before the young English forward scored his first league goal of the season to cap off a "commanding" 4–0 destruction of Burnley at Turf Moor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/burnley-vs-chelsea/report/390848|title=Burnley 0-4 Chelsea: Ross Barkley stars for Blues as they brush Clarets aside|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea then battled to a 3–2 home win over Derby County in the League Cup last 16, with all five goals coming in an eventful first half, with Fikayo Tomori and Cesc Fabregas (along with a Richard Keogh own goal) on target for the Blues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-derby/402317|title = Chelsea 3-2 Derby: Cesc Fabregas scores winner against Frank Lampard's brave side}}</ref>

===November===
Chelsea began November with a 3–1 home win over Crystal Palace, thanks largely to Morata's double.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-c-palace/390860|title = Chelsea 3-1 Crystal Palace: Alvaro Morata guides unbeaten Blues up to second}}</ref> A nervy 1–0 win at BATE followed, with Olivier Giroud scoring his first goal under Maurizio Sarri, sealing a spot in the last 32 of the Europa League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bate-borisov-vs-chelsea/401997|title = BATE 0-1 Chelsea: Olivier Giroud's first goal of the season puts Blues through in Europa League}}</ref> Afterwards, Chelsea extended their unbeaten run of the campaign to eighteen matches after a goalless draw at home with Everton.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-everton/report/390869|title=Chelsea 0-0 Everton: Blues dominate but fail to beat Jordan Pickford|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> However, their unbeaten record under Sarri was halted at that figure, with several defensive lapses seeing them fall to a 3–1 loss at Tottenham.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-chelsea/390883|title = Tottenham 3-1 Chelsea: Maurizio Sarri's unbeaten start ended}}</ref> Chelsea, however, recovered well by securing top spot in their Europa League group with a dominant 4–0 win over PAOK Salonika, with Giroud scoring twice and Callum Hudson-Odoi getting his first senior goal in a convincing display to cap off November.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-paok-snika/report/402022|title=Chelsea 4-0 PAOK: Callum Hudson-Odoi nets first senior goal in easy win|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>

===December===
Chelsea began December with a routine 2–0 home win over Fulham, thanks to goals from Pedro and Loftus-Cheek.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-fulham/390889|title = Chelsea 2-0 Fulham: Pedro, Ruben Loftus-Cheek seal easy victory on Claudio Ranieri's return}}</ref> before losing for just the second time that season, away to Wolves. After Ruben Loftus-Cheek gave Chelsea a first-half lead, the hosts struck back with second-half goals from Raul Jiminez and Diogo Jota to claim a 2–1 win.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/wolves-vs-chelsea/390904|title = Wolves 2-1 Chelsea: Hosts end run of six games without victory}}</ref> Chelsea were underdogs heading into a clash against a Manchester City team who had not lost domestically since April.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/manchester-city-results/2017-18|title=Manchester City (Sky Sports)|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> However, despite being outplayed for large periods of the contest, a rocket-shot from Kante and a looping header from David Luiz sealed a memorable 2–0 win to ensure Chelsea's return to the top four.<ref name="skysports.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-man-city/390911|title = Chelsea 2-0 Manchester City: Pep Guardiola's men lose unbeaten run at Stamford Bridge}}</ref> Chelsea then completed their Europa League group campaign with a 2–2 draw away to MOL Vidi. After going ahead through Willian, an Ethan Ampadu own goal and Loic Nego's sweet volley put the home side ahead, before a late leveller from Giroud sealed a point.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/vidi-vs-chelsea/report/402054|title=MOL Vidi 2-2 Chelsea: Blues lose perfect Europa League record in Hungary|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>
After first-half goals from Pedro and Hazard helped Chelsea battle past a resilient Brighton team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/brighton-vs-chelsea/390917|title = Brighton 1-2 Chelsea: Eden Hazard the difference as Blues hold on for victory}}</ref> Maurizio Sarri's team set up a League Cup semi-final with London rivals Tottenham after scraping past Bournemouth 1–0 in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-bmouth/402810|title = Chelsea 1-0 Bournemouth: Eden Hazard sends Blues into Carabao Cup semi-finals}}</ref> However, this was followed by a frustrating home defeat to Leicester City, with the Foxes becoming the first team to win at Stamford Bridge all year thanks to Jamie Vardy's 51st-minute effort.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-leicester/390930|title = Chelsea 0-1 Leicester: Jamie Vardy secures victory}}</ref> After goals from either side in first-half stoppage-time, Eden Hazard's penalty won the day at Watford,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/watford-vs-chelsea/report/390946|title=Watford 1-2 Chelsea: Eden Hazard double earns Blues victory|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> before 2018 ended on a high for Chelsea after N'Golo Kante scored the only goal at Selhurst Park against Crystal Palace.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/c-palace-vs-chelsea/390949|title = Crystal Palace 0-1 Chelsea: N'Golo Kante strike boosts Blues}}</ref>

===January===
A disappointing goalless draw at home with Southampton was not the best way possible to start the new year,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-soton/390960|title = Chelsea 0-0 Southampton: Maurizio Sarri's side held at home}}</ref> but Chelsea soon secured their first win of 2019 after beating Nottingham Forest 2–0 in the FA Cup third round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-n-forest/403463|title = Chelsea 2-0 Nottingham Forest: Alvaro Morata scores twice in Cesc Fabregas' farewell game}}</ref> However, a 1–0 reverse to Tottenham in the first leg of the League Cup semi-final followed,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-chelsea/403992|title = Tottenham 1-0 Chelsea: Harry Kane scores penalty winner via VAR intervention}}</ref> before goals from Pedro and Willian earned a 2–1 victory over Newcastle United.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-newcastle/390970|title = Chelsea 2-1 Newcastle: Willian's strike seals Blues victory}}</ref>
Chelsea (in fourth) had the gap to fifth closed to three points after Arsenal won 2–0 in a one-sided London derby,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-chelsea/report/390977|title=Arsenal 2-0 Chelsea: Alexandre Lacazette and Laurent Koscielny goals give Gunners win|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> before beating Tottenham 4–2 on penalties after winning 2–1 in the second leg of the League Cup semi-final,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-tottenham/403994|title = Chelsea 2-1 Tottenham (2-2 on agg, 4-2 on pens): Blues reach Carabao Cup final}}</ref> to set up a final against holders Manchester City. They then strolled to a 3–0 win over Sheffield Wednesday in the FA Cup fourth round,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-sheff-wed/405005|title = Chelsea 3-0 Sheffield Wednesday: Callum Hudson-Odoi scores as Blues reach FA Cup fifth round}}</ref> before falling out of the top four after suffering a 4–0 league reverse at Bournemouth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bmouth-vs-chelsea/390988|title = Bournemouth 4-0 Chelsea: Joshua King scores twice as Blues suffer heavy loss}}</ref>

Chelsea only signed two players in January; the first was Juventus` Argentine forward Gonzalo Higuain, who arrived on loan for the remainder of the season, with an option to buy at the end.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/23/gonzalo-higuain-completes-loan-transfer-to-chelsea|title = Gonzalo Higuain completes loan transfer to Chelsea &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club}}</ref> The second was young American prospect Christian Pulisic, who signed from Borussia Dortmund, though was sent back on loan to Germany for the remainder of the campaign.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/2/pulisic-transfer-agreed|title=Pulisic transfer agreed &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club|newspaper=Chelseafc }}</ref> A host of players departed on loan,<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/transfers/january/2019|title = January 2019 Premier League transfers - Latest Transfer Window News}}</ref> among them Alvaro Morata to Spaniards Atletico Madrid and Michy Batshuayi to Fenerbahce.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/26/morata-moves-to-atletico-madrid-on-loan|title = Morata moves to Atletico Madrid on loan &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/1/25-/victor-moses-completes-fenerbahce-loan-move|title = Victor Moses completes Fenerbahce loan move &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club}}</ref> Five players also departed permanently, most notably Cesc Fabregas, who joined French side AS Monaco.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>

===February===
Chelsea returned to fourth after walloping Huddersfield Town 5–0 in the Premier League, with January signing Gonzalo Higuain scoring twice on his home debut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-huddsfld/391000|title = Chelsea 5-0 Huddersfield: Gonzalo Higuain, Eden Hazard star in win}}</ref> However, Chelsea's flaws were exposed after being beaten 6–0 at Manchester City, in their heaviest league defeat since 1992, when they lost 7–0 to Nottingham Forest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/man-city-vs-chelsea/391012|title = Man City 6-0 Chelsea: Sergio Aguero scores another hat-trick as reigning champions hit six of the best}}</ref>
After the City drubbing, Chelsea earned a 2–1 win away to Swedish outfit Malmo FF in the first leg of the Europa League last 32.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/malmo-ff-vs-chelsea/403939|title = Malmo 1-2 Chelsea: Ross Barkley scores first European goal in Europa League last-32 first leg}}</ref> An FA Cup exit to Manchester United was followed by the second leg,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-man-utd/report/405684|title=Chelsea 0-2 Man Utd: Paul Pogba and Ander Herrera goals send United to quarter-finals|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> which Chelsea won 3–0 to secure passage to the last 16.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-malmo-ff/403952|title = Chelsea 3-0 Malmo (5-1 aggregate): Maurizio Sarri's side ease into Europa League last 16}}</ref>
Chelsea then faced Manchester City in the League Cup final, and put in a solid defensive display to draw 0–0. In extra-time, however, manager Sarri attempted to call goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga off, but the Spanish stopper refused to be substituted,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/video/2019/feb/25/kepa-substitution-row-a-misunderstanding-chelsea-manager-maurizio-sarri-says-video|title = Chelsea's Maurizio Sarri: Kepa substitution row a 'misunderstanding' – video|newspaper = The Guardian|date = 25 February 2019}}</ref> and City went on to win 4–3 on penalties.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-man-city/405627|title = Chelsea 0-0 Manchester City (AET - 3-4 on pens): Pep Guardiola's side retain Carabao Cup}}</ref> Chelsea ended February with a critical home match against Tottenham in the league. After taking the lead through Pedro, Chelsea won 2–0 after a Kieran Trippier backpass rolled into his own net.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-tottenham/391032|title = Chelsea 2-0 Tottenham: Pedro and Kieran Trippier own goal give Maurizio Sarri's side fine win}}</ref>

===March===
March began with Higuain scoring his first away goal for Chelsea in a narrow 2–1 success at Fulham,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/fulham-vs-chelsea/391041|title = Fulham 1-2 Chelsea: Gonzalo Higuain and Jorginho secure victory}}</ref> before goals from Pedro, Willian and Hudson-Odoi ensured a 3–0 first leg win over Dynamo Kyiv in the last 16 of the Europa League.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-dynamo-kiev/406351|title = Chelsea 3-0 Dynamo Kiev: Blues put one foot in quarter-finals with convincing win}}</ref> A stoppage-time equalizer from Eden Hazard earned them a point against Wolves,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-wolves/391049|title = Chelsea 1-1 Wolves: Eden Hazard scores injury-time equaliser}}</ref> before Olivier Giroud's first Chelsea hat-trick ensured a memorable 5–0 win away to Dynamo Kyiv, and an 8–0 aggregate victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/dynamo-kiev-vs-chelsea/406359|title = Dynamo Kiev 0-5 Chelsea (Agg: 0-8): Olivier Giroud nets perfect hat-trick in comfortable win}}</ref>
A 2–0 league loss to Everton further dented Chelsea's Champions League qualification hopes,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/everton-vs-chelsea/report/391060|title=Everton 2-0 Chelsea: Toffees dent Blues top-four hopes|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> before March ended with a controversial win at Cardiff City,<ref name="ReferenceB">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/cardiff-vs-chelsea/report/391070|title=Cardiff 1-2 Chelsea: Ruben Loftus-Cheek seals comeback win over unlucky Bluebirds|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> with Cesar Azpilicueta scoring from an offside position and Cardiff having at least "two good penalty shouts."<ref name="ReferenceB"/> waved away.

===April===
Chelsea maintained their 100% league record against Brighton with a 3–0 victory at Stamford Bridge that lifted them to fifth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-brighton/391021|title = Chelsea 3-0 Brighton: Callum Hudson-Odoi impresses as Blues go fifth}}</ref> Eden Hazard scored what would win the Premier League goal of the Month for April with a fantastic solo effort as the forward netted a brace in the 2–0 win over West Ham United.<ref name="premierleague.com"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-west-ham/391078|title = Chelsea 2-0 West Ham: Eden Hazard shines to send Blues third in Premier League}}</ref> A late Marcos Alonso header earned Chelsea a 1–0 away win in the first leg of the Europa League quarter-finals against Czech Slavia Prague,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/slavia-prague-vs-chelsea/report/406469|title=Slavia Prague 0-1 Chelsea: Late Marcos Alonso goal gives Blues victory|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> before second-half goals from Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah saw Chelsea lose 2–0 at Liverpool in the league.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/liverpool-vs-chelsea/391092|title = Liverpool 2-0 Chelsea: Mohamed Salah stunner sends Reds top}}</ref> However, they followed this up with a thrilling 4–3 win against Slavia Prague in the return quarter-final leg of the Europa League, with Chelsea leading 4–1 after 27 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-slavia-prague/report/406471|title=Chelsea 4-3 Slavia Prague (Agg: 5-3) Pedro scores twice in seven-goal thriller|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>
Chelsea then drew with Burnley 2–2, as Kante scored his first goal of 2019 and Higuain adding his fourth for the club. All four goals came in a thrilling opening 24 minutes,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-burnley/report/391100|title=Chelsea 2-2 Burnley: Blues miss opportunity to go third after entertaining draw|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> before April finished with Alonso cancelling out Juan Mata's opener in a 1–1 draw away with Manchester United.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/man-utd-vs-chelsea/report/391113|title=Man Utd 1-1 Chelsea: David de Gea howler gives Chelsea advantage in top-four chase|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>

===May===
May began with a tense 1–1 draw away to German Eintracht Frankfurt in the first leg of the Europa League semi-final, with Pedro lashing home an equalizer just before half-time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/frankfurt-vs-chelsea/406476|title = Eintracht Frankfurt 1-1 Chelsea: Pedro scores vital away goal in Europa League semi-final}}</ref> Chelsea then secured a top-four finish for the first time since 2017, after second-half goals from Ruben Loftus-Cheek, David Luiz and Gonzalo Higuain earned a 3–0 home win against Watford.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-watford/report/391120|title=Chelsea 3-0 Watford: Blues secure Champions League qualification|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea then faced Frankfurt in the second leg of the Europa League semi-final and, after taking the lead through Loftus-Cheek, were forced into extra-time after a second-half goal from Luka Jovic. Cesar Azpilicueta had a goal disallowed for a foul on goalie Trapp in the build-up, before Eden Hazard scored the winning penalty in the shootout to send Chelsea to meet Arsenal's 7–3 aggregate winners over Valencia in the final in Baku, Azerbaijan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-frankfurt/406478|title = Chelsea 1-1 Eintracht Frankfurt (Agg: 2-2, 4-3 on pens) Kepa Arrizabalaga sends Blues to Europa League final}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2019-May-09/valencia-2-4-arsenal-match-report|title = Valencia 2-4 Arsenal (3-7 agg): How it happened | date=9 May 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/11676583/when-is-the-europa-league-final|title = When is the Europa League final?}}</ref>
Chelsea's final day draw at Leicester secured a third-place league finish,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/leicester-vs-chelsea/391131|title = Leicester 0-0 Chelsea: Finishing costs both sides in goalless draw}}</ref> with Chelsea having amassed 72 points from a possible 114.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/premier-league-table/2018|title=Premier League (Sky Sports)|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea collected one individual award for the league campaign, with Eden Hazards 15 assists enough to earn him the Premier League Playmaker Award for the most assists,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1215978|title=Hazard wins 2018/19 Premier League Playmaker of the Season Award|website=Premierleague.com|date=12 May 2019 |access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> whilst also collecting the Chelsea Player of the Year, Players` Player of the Year and Goal of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/05/27/eden-hazard-wins-pfa-fans--player-of-the-year-award|title=EDEN HAZARD WINS PFA FANS' PLAYER OF THE YEAR AWARD &#124; Official Site &#124; Chelsea Football Club|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>
After a 3–0 win away to New England Revolution in a warm-up friendly,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/ne-revolution-vs-chelsea/stats/406415|title=Friendly Match (Sky Sports)|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref> Chelsea faced Arsenal in the UEFA Europa League final. After a tense first half of few openings, Olivier Giroud nodded Chelsea in front on 49 minutes,<ref name="youtube.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=16fOPqI2T_o|title = - YouTube|website = [[YouTube]]}}</ref> and the team soon were ahead 2–0 after Pedro swept home on the hour mark.<ref name="youtube.com"/> Hazard made it 3–0 from the spot before Alex Iwobi pulled on back for Arsenal;<ref name="youtube.com"/> however, a second from Hazard sealed the game ensured a 4–1 win as Chelsea won the Europa League for the second time in their history.This was no thanks to Giroud who was carried by Hazard<ref name="youtube.com"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-arsenal/report/407117|title=Chelsea 4-1 Arsenal: Eden Hazard scores twice in Europa League final|website=Sky Sports|access-date=26 July 2022}}</ref>
